acceptable.ex: Late homework is not acceptable in this class.

accused.ex: She accused her brother of taking her phone.

addition.en: in addition to: as well as
addition.ex: In addition to French, she speaks Italian.

agreed.ex: The teachers agreed to change the timetable.

airspace.ex: The plane entered Spanish airspace at noon.

altered.ex: The town has altered greatly since 1990.

annual.ex: The school holds an annual sports day.

annually.ex: The festival is held annually in May.

another.en: one more of the same kind

apart.ex: Apart from the rain, the trip was perfect.

appearance.en: the act of being seen somewhere
appearance.ex: The sudden appearance of a fox scared the hens.

appetite.en: wish or desire to do something
appetite.ex: Voters have little appetite for higher taxes.

argued.en: gave reasons to show something is true
argued.ex: He argued that the plan was too expensive.

armed.ex: Armed guards stood at the gate.

as.en: in the role or way of

ask.ex: Let's ask the class for their opinions.

asserted.en: stated strongly that something is true
asserted.ex: She asserted that she had done nothing wrong.

example.en: The minister asserted that the plan would save money.
example.zh: 部長斷言該計畫將能節省經費。

note.meaning: 堅定地宣稱；斷言某事為真。
note.usage: 常接 that 子句，語氣比 say 更強烈、正式；assert oneself 指表現自信、維護自身權益。

noteEn.meaning: to say firmly that something is true.
noteEn.usage: Often used as 'assert that...'; stronger and more formal than 'say'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El ministro afirmó que el plan ahorraría dinero.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir con 'assert that'; es más fuerte y formal que 'say'.

noteHi.exampleTr: मंत्री ने ज़ोर देकर कहा कि योजना से पैसे बचेंगे।
noteHi.meaning: दृढ़ता से कहना कि कुछ सच है।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर 'assert that' के साथ; 'say' से अधिक ज़ोरदार और औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 大臣はその計画で費用が節約できると断言した。
noteJa.meaning: 何かが真実だと強く主張する。
noteJa.usage: assert that 〜 の形が多く、say より強く改まった言い方。

noteKo.exampleTr: 장관은 그 계획이 비용을 절감할 것이라고 단언했다.
noteKo.usage: 주로 assert that ~ 형태로 쓰며, say보다 강하고 격식 있는 표현이다.

assessment.en: a careful study to judge something
assessment.ex: The doctor made an assessment of his health.

at.en: in or near a place or time

attack.ex: Hackers tried to attack the bank's computers.

attributable.ex: The fall in sales is attributable to bad weather.

example.en: Most of the delays were attributable to bad weather.
example.zh: 大部分延誤都是惡劣天氣造成的。

note.usage: 固定搭配 be attributable to + 名詞，用於正式說明原因。

noteEn.usage: Use 'be attributable to' + noun, mostly in formal writing.

noteEs.exampleTr: La mayoría de los retrasos se debieron al mal tiempo.
noteEs.usage: Se usa en la estructura 'be attributable to + sustantivo', en registro formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: अधिकांश देरी ख़राब मौसम के कारण हुई।
noteHi.usage: हमेशा 'attributable to + संज्ञा' के रूप में; औपचारिक भाषा में।

noteJa.exampleTr: 遅れのほとんどは悪天候が原因だった。
noteJa.usage: be attributable to + 名詞 の形で、改まった文で原因を述べる。

noteKo.usage: be attributable to + 명사 형태로 격식 있게 원인을 말할 때 쓴다.

autumn.ex: The leaves turn red in autumn.

basis.en: on a … basis: in a … way
basis.ex: We meet on a weekly basis.
basis.zh: on an annual basis：每年一次

become.ex: The roads become icy in winter.

biggest.ex: Money is our biggest problem right now.

bills.en: papers showing money you must pay
bills.ex: We paid the electricity bills yesterday.

biodiversity.en: the variety of living things in a place

break.ex: After a short break, the meeting continued.

cabinet.en: the main group of government ministers

came.ex: The new phone came out last month.

care.ex: He doesn't care about the cost.

catalogued.ex: The museum catalogued all its old coins.

categories.ex: The prizes are split into three categories.

caused.ex: The storm caused a lot of damage.

change.en: climate change: changes in world weather
change.ex: Change can be difficult for some people.

changed.ex: My city has changed a lot.

characterised.en: described as having a certain quality
characterised.ex: Critics characterised the film as boring.

charged.ex: The paper charged the mayor with lying.

citing.en: mentioning as an example or reason
citing.ex: She left the job, citing personal reasons.

climate.en: the usual weather of a place

clockwork.ja: 時計仕掛けのように正確に

commitment.en: being willing to work hard for something
commitment.ex: Her commitment to the team is clear.

communications.ex: The storm cut off communications to the island.

competitiveness.en: ability to compete well with others
competitiveness.ex: Lower costs improve a company's competitiveness.

compiled.ex: She compiled a list of useful websites.

complete.ex: I need to complete this form.

condemned.en: said strongly that something is wrong

conflicts.ex: The region has seen many conflicts.

confronting.ex: The city is confronting a housing shortage.

consultation.ex: The council held a consultation on the new park.

contends.en: says firmly that something is true
contends.ex: He contends that the test was unfair.

example.en: Some experts contend that homework does little good.
example.zh: 一些專家主張家庭作業沒什麼好處。

note.meaning: 主張；堅稱（尤指在爭論中）。
note.usage: contend that 表示提出論點；contend with 則是「應付、對付（困難）」。

noteEn.meaning: to argue or claim that something is true.
noteEn.usage: 'Contend that' means claim; 'contend with' means deal with a problem.

noteEs.exampleTr: Algunos expertos sostienen que los deberes sirven de poco.
noteEs.meaning: sostener o afirmar en una discusión.
noteEs.usage: 'contend that' = sostener; 'contend with' = enfrentarse a un problema.

noteHi.exampleTr: कुछ विशेषज्ञों का दावा है कि गृहकार्य से बहुत कम लाभ होता है।
noteHi.meaning: बहस में कोई बात ज़ोर देकर कहना।
noteHi.usage: 'contend that' = दावा करना; 'contend with' = किसी कठिनाई से निपटना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 宿題はほとんど役に立たないと主張する専門家もいる。
noteJa.usage: contend that 〜 で「〜と主張する」、contend with で「（困難）に対処する」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 일부 전문가들은 숙제가 별 도움이 안 된다고 주장한다.
noteKo.usage: contend that ~은 '~라고 주장하다', contend with는 '(어려움에) 대처하다'.

context.ex: You must understand the historical context.

continually.en: again and again; all the time

continue.ex: The rain will continue all day.

cost.en: cost of living: money needed for basic things
cost.ex: The cost of food keeps rising.

cost-of-living.en: about the price of everyday needs
cost-of-living.ex: Many families face a cost-of-living crisis.

country.ex: Canada is a very large country.

covid.en: Covid-19, a disease that caused a pandemic

crisis.ex: The country faced an economic crisis.

current.ex: The current rules are too strict.

dating.en: dating from: made at that time

delay.en: a time when something is late
delay.ex: There was a long delay at the airport.

department.en: a part of a government or organisation
department.ex: He works in the health department.

dependence.ex: We must reduce our dependence on oil.

described.ex: She described the hotel as dirty.

displaying.ex: The child was displaying signs of tiredness.

disruption.en: a break that stops normal activity
disruption.ex: The storm caused disruption to train services.

document.en: an official written paper or report
document.ex: Please sign the document at the bottom.

does.en: helping verb used in negatives and questions

drone.en: a small flying machine with no pilot
drone.ex: A drone filmed the concert from above.

drones.en: small flying machines with no pilot
drones.ex: Farmers use drones to check their crops.

during.en: at some time in a period

dwindling.ex: The village has a dwindling population.

easier.ex: This road makes the trip easier.

east.en: part of the name Middle East

economic.ex: The country faces serious economic problems.

economy.en: the money and business system of a country
economy.ex: Tourism is important for the local economy.

edition.en: one version of a regularly published report
edition.ex: The new edition of the guide came out today.

either.ex: I don't like coffee, and she doesn't either.

end.en: the last part of a time
end.ex: We will meet again at the end of the month.

energy.en: power such as electricity or gas
energy.ex: Solar panels can lower your energy costs.

entail.en: to include as a necessary part
entail.ex: The job will entail some travel abroad.

example.en: Starting a business entails a lot of hard work.
example.zh: 創業需要付出大量的努力。

note.meaning: 必然涉及；需要（某事作為必要部分）。
note.usage: 後接名詞或動名詞，如 entail doing；多用於正式語境，常見 will entail / would entail。

noteEn.meaning: to involve something as a necessary part.
noteEn.usage: Followed by a noun or -ing form; used in formal writing.

noteEs.exampleTr: Empezar un negocio implica mucho trabajo duro.
noteEs.usage: Va seguido de un sustantivo o un gerundio (entail doing); registro formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: व्यवसाय शुरू करने में बहुत मेहनत शामिल होती है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी चीज़ को आवश्यक रूप से शामिल करना।
noteHi.usage: इसके बाद संज्ञा या -ing रूप आता है; औपचारिक प्रयोग।

noteJa.exampleTr: 起業には多くの努力が伴う。
noteJa.meaning: 必然的に〜を伴う；必要とする。
noteJa.usage: 名詞や動名詞（entail doing）を目的語にとる。フォーマルな表現。

noteKo.usage: 명사나 동명사(entail doing)를 목적어로 취하며 격식체에서 쓰인다.

environment.en: the natural world of land, air and water

environmental.ex: The project had a big environmental impact.

erosion.en: slow loss or damage over time
erosion.ex: Rain caused erosion of the hillside.

escalated.ex: Prices escalated after the war began.

example.en: The argument quickly escalated into a fight.
example.zh: 那場爭吵很快就升級成打架。

note.meaning: （價格、衝突等）急劇上升；逐步升級。
note.usage: 多作不及物動詞，主詞常為 costs、prices、tensions、conflict；也可作及物「使升級」。

noteEn.meaning: to increase quickly or become more serious.
noteEn.usage: Often used with costs, prices or tensions; 'escalate into' something worse.

noteEs.exampleTr: La discusión rápidamente se convirtió en una pelea.
noteEs.usage: Suele usarse con costs, prices, tensions; escalate into = convertirse en algo peor.

noteHi.exampleTr: बहस जल्दी ही लड़ाई में बदल गई।
noteHi.meaning: (क़ीमतें, तनाव आदि) तेज़ी से बढ़ना या गंभीर होना।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर costs, prices, tensions के साथ; escalate into = बढ़कर ... बन जाना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 口論はすぐに殴り合いに発展した。
noteJa.meaning: （価格・対立などが）急上昇する；エスカレートする。
noteJa.usage: costs, prices, tensions などが主語になることが多い。escalate into 〜で「〜に発展する」。

noteKo.usage: costs, prices, tensions 등이 주어로 자주 쓰이며, escalate into ~는 '~로 번지다'.

establishment.en: the act of setting up something new
establishment.ex: The establishment of a new school took two years.

events.en: things that happen, e.g. extreme weather
events.ex: Floods are becoming common events here.

ever.ex: The city is growing ever larger.

examples.en: things that show what you mean
examples.ex: The teacher gave us some examples.

exception.en: something not included in a rule
exception.ex: Everyone came, with the exception of Tom.

exercise.en: an activity done for a purpose
exercise.ex: The survey is an annual exercise.

existing.ex: We will improve the existing system.

exposed.ex: The house is exposed to strong winds.

extreme.ex: Extreme heat closed schools last week.

facing.ex: The problems facing schools are serious.

failed.en: did not do what was expected
failed.ex: He failed to call his mother.

fianna.en: part of an Irish party name
fianna.ja: フィアナ・フォイル（政党）
fianna.zh: Fianna Fáil：共和黨（愛爾蘭政黨）

finalise.en: to complete and agree the last details
finalise.ex: We need to finalise the plans by Friday.

fine.en: part of an Irish party name
fine.zh: Fine Gael：統一黨（愛爾蘭政黨）

flux.ex: The rules are in a state of flux.

followed.ex: One shop cut prices, and others followed suit.
followed.zh: follow suit：跟著照做；如出一轍

fundamental.ex: There is a fundamental problem with the plan.

example.en: Education is fundamental to a country's future.
example.zh: 教育對一個國家的未來至關重要。

note.meaning: 根本的；基本而極重要的。
note.usage: 多置於名詞前，如 a fundamental change/lack；fundamental to 表示「對……至關重要」。

noteEn.meaning: basic and very important; at the deepest level.
noteEn.usage: Usually before a noun; 'fundamental to' means essential for.

noteEs.exampleTr: La educación es fundamental para el futuro de un país.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir delante del sustantivo (a fundamental change); fundamental to = esencial para.

noteHi.exampleTr: शिक्षा किसी देश के भविष्य के लिए मूलभूत है।
noteHi.usage: आमतौर पर संज्ञा से पहले; fundamental to = के लिए अत्यंत आवश्यक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 教育は国の未来にとって不可欠だ。
noteJa.meaning: 根本的な；基本的で非常に重要な。
noteJa.usage: 名詞の前に置くことが多い（a fundamental change）。fundamental to 〜で「〜に不可欠な」。

noteKo.usage: 주로 명사 앞에 쓰이며(a fundamental change), fundamental to ~는 '~에 필수적인'.

further.ex: She further said that costs would rise.

furthermore.ex: The hotel is cheap. Furthermore, it is near the beach.

fáil.en: part of an Irish party name
fáil.ja: フィアナ・フォイル（政党）
fáil.zh: Fianna Fáil：共和黨（愛爾蘭政黨）

gael.en: part of an Irish party name
gael.zh: Fine Gael：統一黨（愛爾蘭政黨）

gap.ex: There was a gap of two years between visits.

gas.en: a fuel used for heating and power
gas.ex: We use gas to heat our house.

geopolitical.en: about politics between countries and regions

global.ex: Climate change is a global problem.

gone.ex: Bus fares have gone up again.

good.ex: The offer holds good until Monday.

government.en: the group of people who rule a country

gravest.ex: This is the gravest danger we face.

green.en: part of the name Green Party

group.en: a number of people working together
group.ex: A small group planned the event.

groups.en: categories that things are put into
groups.ex: The words are sorted into groups.

grown.ex: The town has grown quieter at night.

hazards.ex: Ice on the road is a hazard.

headings.ex: The report has four main headings.

hold-up.ex: Sorry for the hold-up at the airport.

housing.en: homes for people to live in
housing.ex: The city needs more cheap housing.

however.ex: It was cold. However, we went out.

ideas.ex: Send us your ideas for the party.

identified.ex: The study identified three main causes.

identify.ex: Can you identify the bird in this photo?

illustrated.ex: The point was illustrated with a chart.

in.en: inside; at a time or place

indefensible.zh: 站不住腳的；無法辯護的

infrastructure.en: basic systems like power and roads
infrastructure.ex: The country must invest in infrastructure.

insists.en: says firmly that something is true
insists.ex: She insists that she is right.

intelligence.ex: Artificial intelligence can write simple stories.

intended.ex: The course is intended for beginners.

interdepartmental.ex: An interdepartmental team studied the problem.

interest.en: wanting to know or do something
interest.ex: He showed no interest in sport.

international.ex: She works for an international company.

interruption.en: a short stop in something continuous
interruption.ex: The game continued after a brief interruption.

is.en: to exist; to have a quality

issued.ex: The bank issued a warning about fake emails.

iteration.en: one version in a repeated series
iteration.ex: The latest iteration of the app is much faster.

keep.ex: Prices keep going up every month.

kept.ex: The phone kept ringing all morning.

key.ex: Trust is a key part of any friendship.

lack.en: the state of not having enough
lack.ex: The project failed because of a lack of money.

landscape.ex: The political landscape changed after the election.

largest.ex: This is the largest city in the country.

last.ex: I saw her at the last meeting.

latest.ex: Have you read the latest news?

leader.en: the person in charge of a group
leader.ex: The team leader called a short meeting.

linked.ex: Poor sleep is linked to stress.

listed.ex: She listed all the things she needed.

lists.ex: The menu lists every dish and its price.

living.en: cost of living: money needed for daily life
living.ex: The cost of living in big cities is high.

long-term.en: lasting or planned for a long time

look.en: look at: to examine or consider
look.ex: Let's look at the problem again tomorrow.

loomed.ex: Exams loomed as the end of term approached.
loomed.ja: 大きく立ちはだかった

loss.ex: The loss of forests harms wildlife.

lot.ex: I learned a lot from this course.

main.ex: The main problem is the cost.

maintained.en: said firmly that something is true
maintained.ex: He maintained that he had done nothing wrong.

maintains.en: says firmly that something is true
maintains.ex: She maintains that the plan will work.

manage.ex: She manages a team of ten people.

meant.en: meant to be: supposed to be
meant.ex: This road is meant to be finished next month.

meantime.ex: Dinner is almost ready; in the meantime, set the table.

meanwhile.ex: He cooked; meanwhile, she cleaned the kitchen.

micheál.en: first name of the Irish Taoiseach

middle.en: Middle East: region of southwest Asia

ministers.ex: The ministers met to discuss the budget.

more.en: a larger amount; more than: over
more.ex: She has worked here for more than ten years.

most.ex: This is the most beautiful beach I know.

named.ex: The report named three main causes of the problem.

nation's.ex: The nation's capital is very crowded.

natural.ex: Floods are a natural hazard in this area.

nature.en: plants, animals and the natural world
nature.ex: We should protect nature for our children.

neglected.en: failed to do something it should do
neglected.ex: He neglected to lock the door before leaving.

example.en: The landlord neglected to repair the roof.

note.meaning: 疏忽；沒有做到應做的事。
note.usage: neglect to do sth 指「未能做某事」；也可接名詞 neglect sb/sth（忽視、疏於照顧）。

noteEn.meaning: to fail to do something you should do, or fail to care for something.
noteEn.usage: Use 'neglect to do something' or 'neglect someone/something'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El casero no se molestó en reparar el tejado.
noteEs.meaning: descuidar; no hacer lo que se debe.
noteEs.usage: neglect to do algo = no hacer algo; neglect algo/a alguien = descuidarlo.

noteHi.exampleTr: मकान मालिक ने छत की मरम्मत नहीं करवाई।
noteHi.meaning: उपेक्षा करना; जो करना चाहिए वह न करना।
noteHi.usage: neglect to do sth = कुछ करने में चूकना; neglect sb/sth = किसी की देखभाल न करना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 家主は屋根の修理を怠った。
noteJa.meaning: 怠る；すべきことをしない。
noteJa.usage: neglect to do で「〜するのを怠る」、neglect + 名詞で「〜をおろそかにする」。

noteKo.meaning: 소홀히 하다; 해야 할 일을 하지 않다.
noteKo.usage: neglect to do: ~하는 것을 게을리하다; neglect + 명사: ~을 방치하다.

networks.en: connected systems such as power or phone lines
networks.ex: Mobile networks went down during the storm.

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a walk.

new.ex: They opened a new shop in town.

o'gorman.en: surname of the Green Party leader

occurred.ex: The accident occurred late at night.

oil.en: a fuel taken from the ground
oil.ex: The price of oil rose last week.

old.ex: I still have my old phone.

omission.ex: The omission of her name from the list upset her.

example.en: The omission of key facts made the report misleading.
example.zh: 遺漏關鍵事實使這份報告具誤導性。

note.usage: 可指「漏掉的東西」或「未做某事」，常用 the omission of sth。

noteEn.meaning: something left out, or a failure to do something expected.
noteEn.usage: Often used as 'the omission of something'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La omisión de datos clave hizo que el informe fuera engañoso.
noteEs.meaning: omisión; algo que no se hizo o se dejó fuera.
noteEs.usage: Se usa mucho en the omission of algo.

noteHi.exampleTr: मुख्य तथ्यों की चूक ने रिपोर्ट को भ्रामक बना दिया।
noteHi.meaning: चूक; कुछ छोड़ देना या न करना।
noteHi.usage: the omission of sth = किसी चीज़ को छोड़ देना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 重要な事実の欠落により、その報告書は誤解を招くものになった。
noteJa.meaning: 省略；すべきことをしないこと。
noteJa.usage: the omission of 〜 で「〜の欠落・省略」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 핵심 사실의 누락으로 보고서가 오해를 불러일으켰다.
noteKo.meaning: 누락; 해야 할 일을 하지 않음.

onwards.ex: The shop is open from 9 a.m. onwards.

out.ex: The book came out last spring.

oversee.ex: A manager will oversee the new project.

example.en: An independent panel will oversee the election.
example.zh: 一個獨立小組將監督這次選舉。

note.meaning: 監督；督導（工作或計畫的進行）。
note.usage: 及物動詞，後接工作、計畫、改革等；過去式 oversaw，過去分詞 overseen。

noteEn.meaning: to watch and control how work is done.
noteEn.usage: Followed by a task or project; past forms are oversaw and overseen.

noteEs.exampleTr: Un panel independiente supervisará las elecciones.
noteEs.usage: Verbo transitivo; pasado oversaw, participio overseen.

noteHi.exampleTr: एक स्वतंत्र पैनल चुनाव की निगरानी करेगा।
noteHi.meaning: निगरानी करना; काम की देखरेख करना।
noteHi.usage: इसके बाद काम/परियोजना आती है; past: oversaw, overseen।

paragraphs: The Irish Government has not published its National Risk Assessment for more than two years. This report lists the biggest dangers that the country could face. The Department of the Taoiseach prepares it.
The report came out every September from 2014, except for a short break during Covid-19. But there was no new report in September 2025, and there has been no report this September either.

The last report, from 2024, named 24 serious risks in five groups: world politics, the economy, society, the environment and technology. Housing, climate change and artificial intelligence were some of the main worries. It also talked about pandemics, extreme weather and the loss of nature.

Since then, the world has changed a lot. There are wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, and energy prices in Europe have gone up sharply. Important systems for energy and communications are also easier to attack.

Green Party leader Roderic O'Gorman says the delay is not acceptable. He says the risks for Ireland keep changing. He gave two examples: drones seen over Ireland in the past year, and a second rise in the cost of living because the country still depends on oil and gas. He also says the Government does not care about long-term planning.

The Government says it will publish a new report by the end of this year. In September, ministers agreed to look at the old one again. They plan to ask the public and political parties for ideas, and a group from different departments will manage the work. Taoiseach Micheál Martin says the 2024 report is still valid.

The Government has failed to publish Ireland's National Risk Assessment for more than two years. The report, produced by the Department of the Taoiseach, identifies the most serious strategic and natural threats facing the State.
It was published every September from 2014, apart from a gap caused by the Covid-19 pandemic. However, no edition appeared in September 2025, and none has been released this year.

The most recent version, from 2024, listed 24 strategic risks across five categories: geopolitical, economic, social, environmental and technological. Key concerns included housing, climate change and artificial intelligence, as well as weak competitiveness, the threat of a pandemic, biodiversity loss and extreme weather.

Since then, the global situation has shifted considerably. Wars continue in Ukraine and the Middle East, energy costs have soared across the EU, and communications and energy networks have become more vulnerable.

Green Party leader Roderic O'Gorman described the delay as unacceptable for a report that is supposed to be annual. He argued that the risks facing Ireland have kept evolving, pointing to drones spotted in Irish airspace over the past year and a second cost-of-living crisis linked to the country's reliance on fossil fuels. He also accused Fianna Fáil and Fine Gael of showing no interest in long-term planning.

The Government has promised a final National Strategic Risk Assessment 2026 by the end of the year. In September, the Cabinet agreed to review the current document, and it plans a public consultation, submissions from Oireachtas parties and a new interdepartmental group to oversee the update. Meanwhile, Taoiseach Micheál Martin insists that the 2024 assessment remains valid.

For more than two years, the Government has neglected to publish Ireland's National Risk Assessment, the document in which the Department of the Taoiseach sets out the gravest strategic and natural hazards confronting the State.

The assessment appeared like clockwork every September from 2014, save for an interruption during the Covid-19 pandemic. Yet September 2025 came and went without a new edition, and this autumn has followed suit.

The latest iteration, dating from 2024, catalogued 24 strategic risks under five headings: geopolitical, economic, societal, environmental and technological. Housing, climate change and artificial intelligence loomed largest, alongside dwindling competitiveness, the spectre of another pandemic, the erosion of biodiversity and increasingly extreme weather.

The landscape has since been transformed. Conflicts rage on in Ukraine and the Middle East, energy bills across the EU have spiralled, and the infrastructure underpinning communications and power has grown ever more exposed.

Green Party leader Roderic O'Gorman has condemned the hold-up as indefensible for what is meant to be a yearly exercise. Ireland's risk profile, he contends, is in constant flux, as illustrated by drone sightings in Irish skies and a renewed cost-of-living squeeze stemming from the country's dependence on fossil fuels. He further charged Fianna Fáil and Fine Gael with displaying scant appetite for long-term planning.

The Government has pledged to finalise a National Strategic Risk Assessment 2026 before the year is out. Ministers resolved in September to revisit the existing document, with a public consultation, submissions from Oireachtas parties and an interdepartmental group to steer the revision. In the meantime, Taoiseach Micheál Martin maintains that the 2024 assessment still holds good.
